confirmed.suspectedCause: The adapter sets media.prev/next, and app.tsx draws them, only when the player's own buttons exist and are shown (elOf). onKey for Shift+N/P also needs media.next/prev. When YouTube hides them in a small player, both go away. The playlist panel's next item (or the original's keyboard shortcut) could be used instead.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced, three runs. On the playlist watch page at 600 px (twice) and at 640x450@2x (once), Sift's bar was 'Pause|Back 10s|Ahead 10s|Mute|Captions|Full screen|Position in video'. YouTube had hidden .ytp-prev-button and .ytp-next-button inline (style 'display: none;', player not in ytp-small-mode). With focus on Back 10s, Shift+N left v=dQw4w9WgXcQ in place (t 13.9 -> 18.9) both times. The original at 600 px (Sift off with trusted Alt+Shift+S, click on the title, Shift+N) went to v=yPYZpwSpKmA&index=2. At 1280 px, Sift's bar had 'Previous|Next video', and Shift+N went to index=2. The code matches the claim: youtube.ts playerBlock sets prev/next through vis(), which drops buttons whose computed display is none, and app.tsx onKey acts on Shift+N only when media.next is set. One nuance: at 600 px the original shows no Previous or Next buttons either. So the gap against the original is the Shift+N/Shift+P keys, plus F1000's policy, which asks for Previous and Next in Sift's bar on any playlist. Sift's playlist section ('RickAstley - Greatest Hits · 1 / 10') still reaches the next item. This is the same defect as F1000's remaining part.
confirmed.fix: src/content/adapters/youtube.ts playerBlock: when the URL has a list, keep .ytp-prev-button and .ytp-next-button even when YouTube hides them inline at small sizes. Use q(sel, player) without the computed-display check, as the captions button already does. Or fall back to the playlist panel's next and previous ytd-playlist-panel-video-renderer. Check that proxy.click on the hidden button (index.ts H.media 'next'/'prev') still advances the playlist; if not, replay Shift+N or Shift+P to #movie_player.

Shot: /home/nico/projects/sift-test-1/research/shots/r11t1-es-home-indonesian-line.png
confirmed.repro: cd /home/nico/projects/sift-test-1; SIFT_PORT=9461 SIFT_TAB=T1-youtube W=60 bun /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/t1r11/lines.ts 'https://www.youtube.com/?persist_hl=1&hl=es'. Reset with ?persist_hl=1&hl=en.
confirmed.suspectedCause: lineFits passes a same-script line when entryLang cannot reliably tell Indonesian from the page language, and then falls back to 'es'. A cached hit is checked again only with scriptFits and vetLine, not for language. A check that the line's language differs from the page's while matching the title's language could catch this.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed by the stored line and by running Sift's own check. I could not put it on screen myself: in two Spanish home loads (lang es-ES/es-ES, 23 entries), the personalized feed had no Boram entry, and all lines were Spanish. But Sift's IndexedDB cache in this profile holds the value 'Koleksi video Boram tentang hari-hari yang menyenangkan', written 2026-10-27T05:27Z. The English line 'Video collection of Boram's fun days' is a separate entry. In the service worker, chrome.i18n.detectLanguage on that line returns isReliable true, id 100%. I ran src/background/text.ts with that detection: scriptFits(line, latin, title) is true, and entryLang(line, 'es', det, output=true) returns 'es'. So lineFits passes it. Indonesian has no FUNCTION_WORDS list, so entryLang falls back to the page's language. A German line with a reliable 'de' detection is caught (returns 'de'). So any reliably detected Latin-script language without a word list passes. Cached hits get only scriptFits and vetLine, so the line shows again on revisits. The reporter's shot matches.
confirmed.fix: src/background/text.ts entryLang: in output mode, when the detection is reliable, names a Latin-script language other than the page's, and that language has no FUNCTION_WORDS list, return the detected language instead of the page's (or add word lists such as id, tr, pl). Also in src/background/index.ts, check cached hits with lineFits (language), not only scriptFits and vetLine.

confirmed.evidence: Harness (the same extract() the extension runs) on http://127.0.0.1:8799/fx/core-budget.html: the round 11 bundle hits puppeteer's 180 s Runtime.callFunctionOn timeout. The pre-round-10 bundle takes 2617/2151 ms. The same round 11 bundle with marqueeCopies stubbed to return null takes 3333/2592 ms.
